did_you_know.text: Did you know? David organized his army under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, then divided the soldiers into three divisions under Joab, Abishai son of Zeruiah, and Ittai the Gittite.

Did you know? The people asked David not to go into battle himself, because Israel’s enemies would focus on him and his presence in the city would be more helpful to them. David accepted their advice.
Did you know? Although Absalom had led a rebellion against him, David commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently with him, and all the people heard his order.
Did you know? The account says that in the battle in the forest of Ephraim, the forest claimed more lives than the sword, meaning that the terrain played a major role in the defeat of Israel’s army.
Did you know? Absalom was caught when his head became entangled in the branches of a large tree, while the mule he was riding continued on beneath him.

Did you know? One of David’s men refused to harm Absalom because the king had explicitly commanded that he be protected; he even said that he would not disobey the king’s order for a thousand pieces of silver.
Did you know? After Joab thrust three spears into Absalom’s heart, Joab’s ten armor-bearers surrounded him and killed him.
Did you know? The account says that during his lifetime Absalom had erected a monument for himself in the King’s Valley and named it "Absalom’s Monument" to preserve his memory.
Did you know? Joab initially sent the Cushite to bring the news to David, but eventually allowed Ahimaaz to run as well; Ahimaaz chose the route through the plain and outran the Cushite.
Did you know? When David asked the Cushite about Absalom, the messenger replied indirectly that all the king’s enemies would end up like that young man, thereby informing David that Absalom was dead.
